name: Symmetric_SSHI
rationale: The previous SSHI failed primarily on startup time, ripple, and stability, likely due to excessive losses in the 10mH inductor (Rs = 52 Ohm) and a storage capacitor that was too small. A symmetric SSHI uses two inductors and two switches to flip the piezo voltage more efficiently at both peaks. By reducing the inductor value to 1mH, the series resistance drops to 7 Ohm, significantly increasing efficiency and speeding up the cold start. A larger Cout (47uF) is used to minimize peak-to-peak ripple and stabilize the output voltage across all load conditions.
